papers.title: On the skew-curvature power law relationship in a stochastic volatility model with infinite variation L\'evy jumps
papers.abstract: The short-term blow up behaviour of the ATM-IV skew is commonly modelled by either a rough volatility process with small Hurst index or an infinite variation L\'evy process in the log-price dynamics. In this paper, we examine which is the effect of mixed dynamics (i.e. rough volatility and infinite variation L\'evy processes) on the ATM-IV skew and curvature. The results of the paper show that the analysis of the leading terms of the short-time expansion of both ATM-IV skew and curvature allow us to determine, from a mixed dynamics model, which mechanism originates the power-law behaviour on the skew and on the curvature. Apart from showing that the mixed model also originates a power law, it has also key implications in model design and calibration. Numerical evidences for the rough Heston model with CGMY L\'evy jumps are provided.

papers.title: From Alpha to Execution: Trading Horizons, Regimes, and Schedules under Concave Impact and Hurst Scaling
papers.abstract: Classical execution models assume linear impact, diffusive prices, and an exogenous horizon. We study execution under concave power-law impact and Hurst-scaled price fluctuations, and make two contributions. First, we choose the execution horizon by maximizing the Sharpe ratio of the trade's realized P&L. Price moves during the execution window are part of that P&L, so executing more slowly reduces its variance, and because impact is concave it can also lower cost per share. Urgency comes only from alpha realized while the order is being worked. The problem is governed by the signs of two quantities: (i) the duration elasticity of impact $a$, which under a structural prior equals the impact-persistence gap $\beta - H$ and can take either sign; and (ii) the net urgency $\nu$, the rate of alpha realization net of exposure relief. When $\nu$ keeps its sign over the window, an interior optimum exists, to leading order in $T/t_f$, only when both are positive; otherwise the order should be worked at the fastest or slowest admissible pace. In the interior regime the first-order condition involves no impact coefficient, order size or volume, and the objective is flat: for a large-cap example, the window within 1% of maximal Sharpe spans more than an order of magnitude. Second, given the window, we derive the schedule shape by convex programming under an envelope cost. For any increasing per-share cost of delay $w(t)$, the KKT solution is $\phi \propto (\lambda - w(t))_+^{1/\beta}$. For a Hurst-scaled envelope $w \propto t^H$, the normalized schedule depends only on $(\beta, H)$, has a closed form via the incomplete beta function, is front-loaded, and tapers smoothly to zero, saving 10-17% of envelope cost relative to a constant-rate (TWAP) schedule of equal duration. Whether it uses the whole window depends on a single dimensionless robustness level, for which we give a calibration.

papers.title: Pricing Generalized Dispersion Swap for Multi-Asset Stochastic Volatility Models
papers.abstract: This paper develops a generalized variance framework for pricing multi-asset dispersion swap based on the determinant of the instantaneous covariance matrix of asset log-returns. This determinant-based measure captures the joint dispersion of multivariate asset returns while accounting for their dependence structure. We formulate the proposed framework under the Heston and Barndorff-Nielsen-Shephard (BNS) stochastic volatility models, deriving an analytical pricing expression for the three-asset Heston formulation and a tractable approximation for the corresponding BNS formulation. To assess the empirical performance of the proposed approach, we conduct numerical experiments using nine stocks obtained through the quantmod package, randomly partitioned into three groups of three assets. The models are calibrated and evaluated against empirical generalized realized variance across selected time horizons.

papers.title: Consumption-investment under alternative stochastic-integral conventions
papers.abstract: We study the Merton consumption-investment problem when risky asset dynamics are written under stochastic-integral conventions indexed by $\alpha$, interpolating between the It\^o ($\alpha=0$), Stratonovich ($\alpha=1/2$), and H\"anggi-Klimontovich ($\alpha=1$) conventions. Transforming the drift jointly with the convention leaves the optimal policy unchanged; holding the drift coefficient numerically fixed changes the investor's opportunity set. Under logarithmic utility, consumption is unaffected while the optimal portfolio weight shifts by $\alpha V^{-1}d_V$; for a Heston asset, $\pi_t^\ast=\alpha+(\mu-r+\alpha\varrho\xi/2)/V_t$, which can change sign across volatility states. Identifying the convention from return data alone is impossible without additional structural restrictions.
